papers.title: Deep convolutional Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We propose deep convolutional Gaussian processes, a deep Gaussian process architecture with convolutional structure. The model is a principled Bayesian framework for detecting hierarchical combinations of local features for image classification. We demonstrate greatly improved image classification performance compared to current Gaussian process approaches on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets. In particular, we improve CIFAR-10 accuracy by over 10 percentage points.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种深度卷积高斯过程用于图像分类，与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on image classification with deep Gaussian processes, with no application to surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification in engineering design, or biomechanics.

summary_en.motivation: To extend deep Gaussian processes to image classification by incorporating convolutional structure for hierarchical feature learning.
summary_en.method: Proposes deep convolutional Gaussian processes, a Bayesian framework that combines convolutional layers with deep Gaussian processes.
summary_en.result: Achieves substantial accuracy improvements on MNIST and CIFAR-10, with over 10 percentage points gain on CIFAR-10.
summary_en.validation: Validated on standard image classification benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR-10).
